title: Ramjas College Students Dance To 'Meri Jhopdi Ke Bhag' On 'Bhajan Clubbing' Night: 'Yeh Hota Hai Concert' | Viral News - News18
text: Bhajans and clubbing are two worlds that one could never think of coming together. Until now. A recent video doing the rounds on social media shows what many are calling a completely new vibe on campus: “Bhajan Clubbing." And no, this is not a meme or a parody. This happened at one of Delhi University’s most prominent colleges. The viral clip comes from Ramjas College where students were seen fully immersed in a devotional song but with the energy of a live concert. Delhi University’s Ramjas College Becomes Center For ‘Bhajan Clubbing’ In the video, students can be seen raising their hands, clapping singing along and swaying to the music. Instead of EDM drops, the speakers played the popular bhajan Meri Jhopdi Ke Bhag Aaj Khul Jayenge. The atmosphere looked more like a college fest night. Watch The Clip Here What Is ‘Bhajan Clubbing’ And Why Is It Happening? For those wondering how this even started, the event is part of the ‘Vasantotsav 2026’ Bhajan Clubbing series. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta inaugurated the initiative on Tuesday, February 10. Speaking at the event, she said that the aim is to connect the younger generation with India’s cultural roots and spiritual traditions. According to her, bhajan and kirtan form the soul of Indian culture and play an important role in nurturing spiritual consciousness among the youth. She also mentioned that presenting traditional practices in contemporary formats can make them more relatable for young audiences. The 10-day series, which began on February 10, will continue till February 19 across selected Delhi University colleges and the University Stadium complex. An official statement noted that the idea is to bring devotion, culture and youthful energy together on one common platform, Press Trust of India reported. Minister for Art, Culture, Language and Tourism, Kapil Mishra, added that the programme draws inspiration from a larger push to promote Indian culture and youth participation. The broader goal is to strengthen Delhi’s position as a hub of art and culture. Full Schedule And Participating Artists As per the reports, the Bhajan Clubbing series features multiple artists and bands performing across different campuses. Leela performed at Ramjas College on February 10, followed by Raghav Raja at Deen Dayal Upadhyay College on February 11. India Music Collective will take the stage at ARSD College today while Sadho Band will perform at Shaheed Sukhdev College the same day. Rahasya will perform at Shyamlal College on February 13 and Keshavam will appear at PGDAV College on the same date. Keshavam is also scheduled to perform at the University Stadium on February 16. The series will wrap up with SAM at Miranda House on February 19.
